tools.name: siemens_assets
tools.description: Finds publicly released Siemens media in the Web Asset Pool: photos, videos, PDFs and other documents, audio and icons. Use it when the user needs a picture, video, logo, icon or downloadable document, for example for a presentation, article or web page. Each result includes the usage rights (unlimited, limited or restricted), whether approval is required, the required credit line, a preview image and download URLs in several sizes (small, medium, large, original). Always tell the user the usage rights and credit before they reuse an asset. Filter with usageRights "UNLIMITED" when the asset is for external or third-party use. Do not use it for text answers about Siemens (use siemens_search) or for developer documentation (use siemens_developer_search).

query.description: Keywords describing the asset content, in English. Examples: "wind turbine offshore", "SIMATIC S7-1500", "factory automation robot", "Siemens logo". Use * for partial matches, for example "turbin*".

assetType.description: Kind of asset. Default "ALL". Use "IMAGES" for photos and illustrations, "VIDEOS", "DOCUMENTS" for PDFs and office files, "AUDIO", or "ICONS".

collection.description: Collection to search. Default "ALL" (the main Siemens DAM). "PRESS" for press photos, "ENERGY" for Siemens Energy media.

usageRights.description: Only return assets with this usage-rights level. Default "ANY". "UNLIMITED": Siemens holds all rights including transfer to third parties. "LIMITED": usable with limitations. "RESTRICTED": not for external material.

imageSize.description: Filter images by original resolution. Default "ANY". "SMALL": under 1024x1024 px, "MEDIUM": over 1024x1024 px, "LARGE": over 2448x2448 px (print quality). Every result still offers several download sizes.

orientation.description: Filter images and videos by orientation. Default "ANY".

maxResults.description: Assets to return in this call. Default 10, range 1-50.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first asset, for paging. Default 0. Pass "next_offset" from the previous response.

response_format.description: Result verbosity. "concise" (default) returns only the fields needed to answer and cite (title, url, short description). "detailed" adds secondary metadata such as scores, thumbnails and keywords. Use "detailed" only when you need those fields.

tools.name: siemens_developer_search
tools.description: Searches the Siemens Developer Portal (developer.siemens.com): API references, SDK guides, authentication, getting-started tutorials and changelogs for Siemens platforms such as Insights Hub, Industrial Edge, Building X, Polarion, Senseye and the Industrial AI Suite. Use it for technical questions about Siemens APIs and developer tools ("How do I authenticate against the Insights Hub API?", "Industrial Edge app SDK"). Returns the best-matching documentation sections with url and a snippet; read a full page with siemens_get_web_content. Do not use it for marketing, company or product-catalog questions (use siemens_search).

query.description: Technical keywords or question. Examples: "OAuth token technical user", "time series API", "edge app docker compose", "webhook events".

product.description: Restrict to one product area, by name or slug. Examples: "insights-hub", "industrial-edge", "building-x-openness", "polarion", "senseye". Omit to search everything. An unknown value (no product area, for example "teamcenter") is dropped: every area is searched with the name added to the keywords, and "hint" lists the valid product areas.

maxResults.description: Documentation sections to return. Default 8, range 1-25.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first result, for paging. Default 0. Pass "next_offset" from the previous response.

portalUrl.description: Base URL of another Siemens Developer Portal instance, for example a merge request review deployment (https://developer.code.siemens.io/...). Must be https and on the server allowlist. Omit for https://developer.siemens.com/.

response_format.description: Result verbosity. "concise" (default) returns only the fields needed to answer and cite (title, url, short description). "detailed" adds secondary metadata such as scores, thumbnails and keywords. Use "detailed" only when you need those fields.

tools.name: siemens_product_datasheet
tools.description: Returns the technical datasheet of one Siemens industry product by its article number (MLFB, for example "6EP3436-8SB00-0AY0") as structured data: sections of properties with values and units (supply voltage, currents, power loss, dimensions, ambient conditions, ...), eClass and ETIM classes and certificates. Use it to check ratings, compare products or verify that devices fit together, for example summing the 24 V DC current of controllers against a power supply rating. When the user only names a product family or a rating, find the article number first with siemens_search and scope "articles". Some product families publish their data only as PDF: then "hasTechnicalData" is false; give the user "datasheetPdfUrl" and do not guess values. When the datasheet service has no datasheet or is slow, the result is the SiePortal catalog entry ("dataSource": "sieportal": description and product page only); an unknown number returns close article numbers. Do not use it for prices, availability or delivery times, which it does not return, or for non-Siemens products.

articleNumber.description: Siemens article number (MLFB) as in the catalog, for example "6ES7214-1AG40-0XB0", "3RV2021-4EA10" or "BPZ:QAA2061". Case and spaces do not matter; ordering options after "-Z" ("7MC8005-3CE10-2HG0-Z C11+G12") are split off and returned as "orderingOptions".

language.description: Datasheet language: en (default), de, fr, es, it or zh. Property names and text values are translated; numbers and units stay the same.

section.description: Only return sections whose name contains this text (case-insensitive), for example "supply voltage" or "ambient". Omit for the full datasheet; "availableSections" lists all names.

tools.name: siemens_search
tools.description: The search tool for any question about Siemens: products, industries, news, references, contacts. "scope" picks what comes back. "all" (default): an AI answer with sources, siemens.com pages ("results"), product family pages ("products"), orderable SiePortal articles ("articles") and Xcelerator Marketplace partner offerings ("partners"). Use it first. Other scopes return one list. "articles" finds article numbers (MLFB) for siemens_product_datasheet. "products" filters the product catalog by "industry", "topic", "seller". "partners": third-party offerings, never Siemens products; "sellers": partner firms, by "sellerRegion" or "motion". "references": customer references by "industry", "country", "customer". "contacts": support contacts by "country". "documents": Smart Infrastructure manuals. "podcasts": siemens.fm podcast episodes. "collection" limits pages and answer to sources ("resources": webinars, white papers; "news"...), one or a list. Read a page in full with siemens_get_web_content. Do not use it for image, video or logo files (siemens_assets) or API docs (siemens_developer_search). Results are public Siemens content only. Cite the returned URLs; do not invent links.

query.description: What to search for, in natural language or keywords. Examples: "What is Teamcenter?", "SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU", "digital twin in automotive manufacturing". Do not add years or site names; the search already covers siemens.com. Required for every scope except "contacts", where "country" alone lists the contacts of a country. For news or press releases use "collection" "news" or "press" (or ["press","news"]).

scope.description: What to return: "all" (default: answer, pages, products, articles and partner offerings), "pages" (siemens.com content pages, with the AI answer on the first page), "products" (product family pages and articles; with "industry", "topic" or "seller" the offerings of the siemens.com product catalog, Siemens' and partners', without articles), "articles" (orderable SiePortal articles with article numbers) or "partners" (third-party offerings on the Siemens Xcelerator Marketplace, with facets), "sellers" (partner companies of the Siemens Ecosystem Explorer, with facets; companies, not products, so a product name finds nothing here (use "products" or "articles"); for partner companies that offer services such as implementation or support use "motion" "Service") or "references" (customer references from references.siemens.com through the platform's keyword search, with filters and facets; put one or two keywords such as a product into "query" and industry, country or customer into the filters) or "contacts" (Siemens support contacts per country from contact.siemens.com: functional mailboxes and hotlines for installation, technical support, spare parts, repairs, training and eBusiness, filtered by "country", "department" and "competence"; a country served by a hub country returns the hub's contacts; not for fault codes or technical questions, use "pages" or "documents") or "documents" (technical product documents from sid.siemens.com, Smart Infrastructure only (building automation, HVAC, fire safety, security: Desigo, Cerberus, Sinorix, Acvatix, KNX GAMMA, ...): data sheets, installation, mounting and operating instructions, manuals and declarations as PDFs and online manuals, by keyword or article number, filtered by "docType" and "product"; read one in full with siemens_get_web_content and its read_url. Not for SIMATIC, SINAMICS or Siemens software (a SIMATIC query returns building documents that mention it), and not for words like "webinar", "video" or "white paper", which match unrelated building documents; use collection "resources" for those) or "podcasts" (public Siemens podcasts from siemens.fm through its AI search: "episodes" ranked by meaning over transcripts, titles and descriptions, each with matching transcript snippets and timestamps, plus matching "podcasts" (shows); "language" keeps episodes in that language, omit it for all languages; one page, no "offset"; read an episode's full description (hosts, guests, speakers) and transcript with siemens_get_web_content and its "url"; internal podcasts are never included).

collection.description: Search only these content collections, one name or a list (["press","news"] for press releases and news articles; use "news" or "press" for any question about Siemens news or press releases): "siemens_com" (web pages of www.siemens.com (products, solutions, industries, company, insights, success stories): 38 country sites with one language each, English only for "US" and "GB", "GLOBAL" searches the US site), "mobility" (web pages of mobility.siemens.com (rail vehicles, rail infrastructure, signaling, services, Mobility newsroom): "GLOBAL" in English and German plus about 70 country sites), "news" (news articles and stories from news.siemens.com, same country sites as siemens_com), "press" (press releases and features from press.siemens.com: "GLOBAL" in English and German plus country releases), "resources" (webinars (webinars.sw.siemens.com) and white papers, case studies, e-books, videos, fact sheets, infographics and brochures (resources.sw.siemens.com), mostly Siemens Digital Industries Software (Teamcenter, NX, Simcenter, Opcenter, Mendix) plus some automation topics (TIA Portal, SIMATIC); same country sites as siemens_com. Use it for webinar, white paper, fact sheet, case study or video questions about these products), "advanta" (consulting offerings, client cases and blog of Siemens Advanta (siemens-advanta.com): English, "GLOBAL" only), "references" (customer references and success stories from references.siemens.com (externally released projects only)), "trainings" (training courses from SITRAIN (sitrain.siemens.com) and Siemens Digital Industries Software training (training.plm.automation.siemens.com). SITRAIN has sites for 29 countries (not US, CN, AT or KR); other countries get the courses of the site in their language (English: GB)), "blogs" (blog posts of Siemens Digital Industries Software from blogs.sw.siemens.com, including its podcast pages (siemens.fm podcasts are scope "podcasts"), and community pages, events and articles from ecosystem.siemens.com: English only), "software" (product sites of Siemens software: Solid Edge (solidedge.siemens.com, English plus 10 languages), Brightly asset management (www.assetmanagement.siemens.com) and free software trials (trials.sw.siemens.com), the last two English only), "events" (event pages of Siemens Digital Industries Software from events.sw.siemens.com (Realize LIVE and other events): English only, check the dates on the page), "careers" (apprenticeship and internship offers of Siemens in Germany from www.ausbildung.siemens.com, not job ads: German only, other languages are searched in German), "siemensstadt" (the Siemensstadt Square district project in Berlin from www.siemensstadt.siemens.com: English and German). Omit to search all Siemens content. Implies scope "pages" (an AI answer from the collections on the first page, none for "press", "news", "events" and "careers", then paged results); other scopes reject it. "region" works as everywhere else: "GLOBAL" for international content or a country code.

industry.description: Scopes "partners", "products", "sellers" and "references": keep results of this industry, case-insensitive. Partners, products and sellers share the ecosystem values ("Automotive", "Machine building", "Food and beverages"); references use their own ("Automotive", "Consumer Packaged Goods / Beverage", "Beverage"). Valid values are in "facets.industries" of that scope.

topic.description: Scopes "partners", "products" and "sellers": keep results tagged with this topic, case-insensitive. Examples: "Sustainability", "Efficiency", "Cybersecurity", "Asset management". Valid values are in "facets.topics".

seller.description: Scopes "products" and "partners": keep offerings of this seller, case-insensitive: a Siemens unit ("Siemens", "Siemens Industry Software", "Siemens Advanta") or a partner ("CLEVR", "DMG MORI"). Valid values are in "facets.sellers".

motion.description: Scope "sellers" only: how the partner works with Siemens. "Build" (builds solutions on Siemens technology), "Service" (implements and supports; use it for partner companies that offer services), "Sell" (resells).

sellerRegion.description: Scopes "partners" and "sellers": keep partners that serve this country or region, case-insensitive. Examples: "Germany", "USA", "United Kingdom", "India". Valid values are listed in "facets.seller_regions".

country.description: Scopes "references" and "contacts". References: country of the project, in English ("Germany", "China", "United States of America"; valid values in "facets.countries"). Contacts: the country whose Siemens contacts to list, as ISO code or English name ("DE", "Germany", "UK").

portfolio.description: Scope "references" only: Siemens portfolio, or "portfolio / area". Examples: "Digital Industries / Industrial automation", "Smart Infrastructure / Fire Safety". Valid values are in "facets.portfolios".

organization.description: Scope "references" only: Siemens business that contributed the reference, by code or name. Examples: "DI", "Smart Infrastructure", "SI B", "Siemens Mobility". Valid values are in "facets.organizations".

tag.description: Scope "references" only: Special tag. Examples: "Sustainability", "Siemens Xcelerator". Valid values are in "facets.tags".

customer.description: Scope "references" only: Customer name or part of it, case-insensitive. Examples: "BMW", "Heineken".

department.description: Scope "contacts" only: Siemens business, case-insensitive, part of the name is enough. Example: "Digital Industry". Valid values are in "facets.departments".

docType.description: Scope "documents" only: document type, case-insensitive, part of the name is enough. Examples: "Data Sheet", "Installation Instructions", "Operating Instructions", "Technical Manual", "Declaration of Conformity". Valid values are in "facets.doc_types".

product.description: Scope "documents" only: product or product line, case-insensitive, part of the name is enough. Examples: "Desigo CC", "Cerberus PACE", "Climatix", "Building X". Valid values are in "facets.products" and "facets.product_lines".

competence.description: Scope "contacts" only: what the contact handles, case-insensitive, part of the name is enough. Values: "Installation, troubleshooting", "Technical support, including licenses", "Replacement parts", "Warranty & repairs", "Training & education options", "eBusiness Consultants"; see "facets.competences".

language.description: Two-letter content language code, uppercase. Default "EN". Examples: "EN", "DE", "FR", "ES", "ZH". Use the language the user writes in when Siemens publishes content in it. A country site may publish only its own language (www.siemens.com Germany only "DE"); a collection search names the languages that exist.

region.description: Country/region of the content, uppercase. Default "GLOBAL" (international pages). ISO country codes ("DE", "US", "GB", "IN", "CN"; "UK" is read as "GB"), also "ASEAN" and "MEA". Only set a country when the user asks about that market.

summaryLevel.description: Length of the AI answer for scope "all" and on the first page of scope "pages" (with or without "collection"). Default "medium". Use "short" for quick facts, "detailed" for explanations. "none" skips the AI answer ("answer" is null) and returns the lists only, a few seconds faster; use it when you only need the results.

maxResults.description: Results to return. Default 10. Scope "all": total of pages and products (about 60/40, range 2-30), plus as many articles and partner offerings as products. "pages": range 1-50. "products", "articles", "partners", "references", "contacts" and "documents": range 1-30. "podcasts": episodes, range 1-20.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first result to return, for paging. Default 0. To get the next page, pass the "next_offset" value from the previous response.

response_format.description: Result verbosity. "concise" (default) returns only the fields needed to answer and cite (title, url, short description). "detailed" adds secondary metadata such as scores, thumbnails and keywords. Use "detailed" only when you need those fields.

tools.name: siemens_get_web_content
tools.description: Fetches one public page on siemens.com, siemens.de or siemens.net (including developer.siemens.com) and returns its main content as clean markdown, without navigation, headers and footers. Use it after siemens_search or siemens_developer_search to read a result in full, or when the user gives you a Siemens URL. Long pages are returned in chunks: if "next_offset" is not null, call again with the same url and offset set to next_offset. siemens.com pages are read through the CommsCloud Markdown API, which renders JavaScript, converts PDFs and reads SiePortal pages; if it fails, the page is fetched directly. "backend" says which path was used. Not every product on siemens.com is a Siemens product: if "provider.is_marketplace_offering" is true, the offering belongs to "provider.name" (a partner on the Siemens Xcelerator Marketplace), so attribute it to that partner and never call it a Siemens product. If "provider" is null, the seller is unknown; make no attribution claim. A public siemens.fm episode "url" (scope "podcasts") returns its full description (hosts, guests) and transcript. Do not use it to search (use siemens_search) or for other websites; other domains are rejected.

url.description: Absolute https URL of a Siemens page or a public siemens.fm podcast or episode page, usually taken from a search result. Example: "https://www.siemens.com/global/en/products/automation/systems/industrial/plc/s7-1500.html".

maxLength.description: Maximum characters of markdown to return in this call. Default 12000. Lower it when you only need the beginning of a page.

offset.description: Character offset to continue reading a long page. Default 0. Pass "next_offset" from the previous response.

render.description: Omit (recommended) or true: read the page through the Markdown API, which always renders it in a browser; if the API fails, fetch it over HTTP and render it in AgentCore Browser when it has almost no text (true: always render on that fallback, slower). false: plain HTTP fetch only, no browser and no Markdown API.
